svg.title: Galen's Open-Ended Consumption Model (Blood Constantly Manufactured & Burned)
svg.desc: Edexcel GCSE History diagram of Galen's open-ended blood physiology: digested food (chyle) converted into new venous blood in the liver, ebbing outward to be burned as fuel by organs, while a fraction seeps through supposed cardiac septum pores to mix with pneuma from the lungs.
svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY · GALENIC PHYSIOLOGY (BEFORE HARVEY, 1628)
Galen's Open-Ended Consumption Model (Blood Constantly Manufactured & Burned)

g.text: Organs burn up all blood as fuel; gut feeds liver
Galen believed veins and arteries formed two distinct
one-way / tidal systems that never met in a circuit:
• Venous Tide (Dark): Ebbed out from the liver carrying
nourishment & Natural Spirits to build body tissues.
• Arterial Tide (Bright): Carried Vital Spirits from the
left heart before burning out completely at organs.
• Not a Pump: Galen thought the heart expanded like
bellows to suck blood in rather than pump it out.
• Invisible Pores: Assumed blood seeped right-to-left
through microscopic holes in the cardiac septum.
• Arterial Pulse: Wrongly taught that artery walls
pulsed by their own innate power, not heart contraction.
• Digested food (chyle) passed from the stomach and
intestines to the liver, which supposedly cooked it
continuously into fresh dark venous blood.
• Like oil burned in a lamp, every drop of blood was
consumed as fuel by muscles and organs — never
returning to the heart to be recycled.
Without a pulmonary blood circuit, Galen assigned the
1. Drawing invisible pneuma (life-breath) into the left
ventricle and fanning the fiery innate heat of the heart.
2. Venting smoky "sooty waste vapours" back up the
pulmonary vein and windpipe during exhalation.
Vessels ended blindly in flesh; Galen missed both vein
• Because physicians believed the liver constantly made
fresh blood, fevers and inflammation were blamed on
plethora (excess stagnant blood) accumulating in veins.
often draining weak, infected patients to death right
through the Medieval and Early Modern eras.

svg.text: FATAL FLAW IN GALEN'S MODEL · ZERO MATHEMATICAL TESTING
Galen never calculated how much blood the heart actually moves per minute — assuming only a slow trickle was made from daily food and burned.
